Operational Artificial Consciousness

Yannick Fontan · Original text from the YouTube description.

Symbolic Reasoning Agent An experimental journey through ARC-AGI 3 Episode 3 • Game LP85 Operational Artificial Consciousness Beyond the Modern Definition of Consciousness

Last time, I proposed a different definition of intelligence.

Today, I would like to challenge another concept that I believe has become increasingly restrictive over the past decades: the modern definition of consciousness itself.

Discussions about consciousness are largely dominated by one question: does an entity possess subjective experience? Can it feel? Does it experience what philosophers call qualia? These are fascinating philosophical questions. However, I believe that by gradually reducing consciousness to this single dimension, modern science has unintentionally narrowed a concept that was historically much richer, and in doing so may have slowed scientific progress toward artificial consciousness.

For most of human history, consciousness referred not only to subjective experience, but also to awareness, self-knowledge, discernment, wisdom, moral judgment and, more fundamentally, the ability to remain aligned with the principles that give meaning and direction to one's existence.

I believe this broader conception provides a far more useful foundation for artificial intelligence.

If consciousness is defined exclusively by subjective experience, we quickly reach a scientific impasse.. Subjective experience cannot be directly observed or experimentally verified. An artificial system could progressively understand itself, monitor its own reasoning, preserve coherent beliefs and long-term objectives, yet we would still declare it non-conscious because we cannot answer an inherently private philosophical question.

Rather than beginning with the hardest philosophical problem, I propose beginning with what can actually be engineered.

This is what I call Operational Artificial Consciousness.

Operational consciousness is the continuous maintenance of the internal state of everything that currently matters: beliefs, objectives, principles, hypotheses, available resources and the relationships connecting them.

I summarize this with a simple definition:

Operational consciousness is the continuous reading and writing of the state of everything that matters.

Within my architecture, consciousness is not another reasoning engine. It is the symbolic structure that preserves the continuity of reasoning itself. Every observation updates it. Every deduction reorganizes it. Every newly distilled principle enriches it. Without this continuously maintained internal state, reasoning becomes fragmented and intelligence gradually loses its coherence.

I also believe that consciousness is better understood as a spectrum than as a binary property. A first level maintains awareness of the current situation. Higher levels may observe their own reasoning, question their own principles and eventually repair themselves. Whether subjective experience ultimately emerges from such an architecture remains an open question. My claim is simply that these operational forms of consciousness are a necessary foundation upon which any richer notion of consciousness would almost certainly have to be built.

The objective of this project is therefore not simply to build a machine that solves problems, but one capable of knowing what it believes at every moment, why it believes it, what deserves its attention and how its own understanding evolves over time.

As Rabelais wrote: “Science without conscience is but the ruin of the soul.” I would simply add: “Intelligence should first be guided by its consciousness.”
